questions.stem:
At schematic design, an owner wants a cost estimate organized by building systems (substructure, shell, interiors, services) to compare two structural and envelope alternatives.

Which classification system should the estimator use?

options.explanation: Correct. UniFormat organizes cost by building elements and systems, which suits early estimates and comparing alternatives.
MasterFormat organizes by work results. It suits detailed estimates once specifications exist.
OmniClass is a broad classification framework, not the usual basis for elemental estimates.
UDS organizes drawing sets, not cost estimates.

questions.explanation: Early, system-level comparison → UniFormat. Specification-level detail → MasterFormat.

questions.stem:
A firm adopts the U.S. National CAD Standard for sheet numbering.

What does sheet A-301 most likely contain?

options.explanation: Correct. A = architectural; 3 = sections; 01 = sequence.

options.text: The third architectural floor plan sheet
options.explanation: Plans use sheet type 1, so the third plan sheet would be A-103.
Details use sheet type 5 (A-501).

options.text: The architectural site plan for Building 3
options.explanation: UDS sheet numbers encode discipline, sheet type and sequence, not building numbers.

questions.explanation: UDS: discipline + sheet type (0 general, 1 plans, 2 elevations, 3 sections, 4 large-scale, 5 details, 6 schedules) + sequence.
questions.confidenceNote: Sheet-type digits per NCS/UDS as I know them; confirm against the current NCS version.

questions.stem:
A firm's last three projects generated many RFIs from conflicts between architectural, structural and MEP documents.

Which firm-wide process changes would best reduce these conflicts?

options.text: Adopt a BIM execution plan with exchange schedules and LOD by milestone
options.explanation: Correct. Clear modeling responsibilities and exchange timing reduce coordination gaps.

options.text: Run scheduled clash detection before each issue
options.explanation: Correct. Routine clash detection catches conflicts before documents go out.

options.text: Require independent QC review before permit and bid sets
options.explanation: Correct. A fresh reviewer finds errors the project team misses.

options.text: Let each consultant use its own sheet numbering
options.explanation: Inconsistent standards make coordination and review harder.

options.text: Rely on the contractor's coordination drawings
options.explanation: Finding conflicts during construction is the costliest way to coordinate.

options.text: Exchange consultant files only at final submission
options.explanation: Late exchange leaves no time to resolve conflicts during design.

questions.explanation: Coordination quality = defined responsibilities + scheduled exchanges + systematic QC.

questions.stem:
A historic warehouse will become apartments. The owner wants to keep its character-defining features while adding modern systems and new interior layouts.

Which Secretary of the Interior's treatment applies?

options.explanation: Correct. Rehabilitation allows compatible alterations and additions for a new use while preserving historic character (36 C.F.R. §68.2).
Restoration depicts the property at a particular period and removes later features.
Preservation sustains existing form and materials with minimal change, which isn't enough for a conversion.
Reconstruction recreates a non-surviving building with new construction.

questions.stem:
A specifier is drafting a CSI-format section for a curtain-wall system.

In which part of the section do installation requirements and field quality control belong?

options.explanation: Part 1 covers administrative requirements: submittals, quality assurance, warranties.
Part 2 covers manufacturers, materials and fabrication.
Correct. Part 3 covers examination, preparation, installation, field quality control, cleaning and protection.
Division 01 holds project-wide requirements, not section-specific installation.

questions.explanation: Part 1 General · Part 2 Products · Part 3 Execution.

questions.stem:
A design-assist mechanical contractor needs model elements accurate enough to fabricate and install ductwork.

Which level of development is required for those elements?

options.explanation: LOD 200 is approximate geometry, suitable for design studies.
LOD 300 is precise design geometry, but not fabrication detail.
Correct. LOD 400 includes detail for fabrication, assembly and installation.
LOD 500 is field-verified as-built information.

questions.explanation: LOD 100 conceptual · 200 approximate · 300 precise · 350 interfaces · 400 fabrication · 500 field-verified.
questions.confidenceNote: LOD definitions per the BIMForum LOD Specification as I know it; confirm in the current edition.

questions.stem:
A firm is starting its first renovation inside an occupied hospital.

Which process adjustments are most important?

options.text: Detailed phasing developed with facility staff
options.explanation: Correct. Work in occupied hospitals must be phased to keep operations running.
Correct. Construction must protect patients from dust and contaminants.
Correct. Healthcare projects face added regulatory review that affects schedule and design.
Healthcare has requirements that standard commercial specifications may not meet.

options.text: A single bid package with continuous closure
options.explanation: Occupied hospitals usually can't close. Phased packages keep operations running.

options.text: Phasing left entirely to the contractor
options.explanation: Phasing shapes the documents and operations, so the architect must help plan it.

questions.explanation: Project type changes the process: healthcare means phasing, infection control and regulatory coordination.

questions.stem:
An architect wants the specification to require that a roof assembly resist a stated wind uplift and pass a specified water test, leaving the choice of products to the contractor.

Which specification method is this?

options.explanation: Correct. Performance specifications state required results and test criteria.
Descriptive specifications detail materials and installation rather than results.
Closed proprietary specifications name specific products with no substitutions.
Reference standard specifications rely on cited standards for materials or workmanship, not project-specific outcomes.

questions.explanation: Performance = what it must do. Descriptive = what it is and how to install it.

questions.stem:
A firm is writing a records-retention policy for project files, including correspondence, meeting minutes and field reports.

Which retention period best protects the firm against late claims?

options.text: Through the statute of repose and claim periods
options.explanation: Correct. Records are key defense evidence and should be kept as long as claims can be brought.

options.text: Seven years, matching typical tax-record practice
options.explanation: Tax-record periods don't match construction-claim exposure.

options.text: Until the architect receives final payment
options.explanation: Claims can arise many years after final payment.
Correspondence and field reports are often the most important defense records.

questions.explanation: Retention should match claim exposure (repose + contract limits, e.g., B101-2017's 10-year outer limit).

questions.stem:
A retail client builds about 30 stores a year from a prototype, each adapted to a different site and jurisdiction.

Which practice-wide resource most improves efficiency and consistency?

options.text: Controlled prototype standards and a site checklist
options.explanation: Correct. Version-controlled prototype documents plus a site process keep stores consistent and locally compliant.

options.text: A custom design for each store
options.explanation: Custom design for each store defeats the purpose of a prototype program.

options.text: The previous store's drawings with an updated title block
options.explanation: Each site has its own code, zoning and conditions that must be reviewed.

options.text: Separate prototype versions kept by each project team
options.explanation: Multiple uncontrolled versions lead to errors and inconsistency.

questions.explanation: Repetitive programs → controlled standards + site-adaptation procedures (NCARB 5.3 for sealing prototypical documents).
